strategies.name: break_and_retest_continuation
strategies.entry_summary: Identify an obvious key level such as pre-market high/low, previous day high/low, or the 30-minute opening range high/low. Enter only after price breaks the level with strong momentum and volume, then retests it and shows confirmation that the level is holding in the breakout direction: bullish cand
strategies.exit_summary: Place the stop on the opposite side of the breakout level, often just beyond the confirmation candle / break area. Target the next obvious area of liquidity such as a previous high/low or supply/demand zone; the speaker also mentions trimming and moving the remainder to breakeven in some examples.

variants.timeframe_note: Examples shown on 5-minute and 2-minute charts; also references Asia session and New York session contexts
variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: After a strong break above resistance, wait for the retest to hold as support and use bullish price action such as long
variants.target_note: Next obvious liquidity above, such as previous high or pre-market high; sometimes trim partials and move rest to breake
variants.transcript_quote: Price breaks above a key level, it comes back, it retests that level, and it holds it, and it continues in the original direction.

variants.timeframe_note: Examples shown on 5-minute and 2-minute charts; also references Asia session and New York session contexts
variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: After a strong break below support, wait for the retest to hold as resistance and use bearish price action such as long
variants.target_note: Next obvious liquidity below, such as previous low or another demand/liquidity area; sometimes trim partials and move r
variants.transcript_quote: Price ends up breaking below the support, well now we have the break, we're waiting for price to come back up and retest it as resistance. If it can

result.enumeration_note: The video teaches one break-and-retest continuation skeleton; long and short executions are opposite-direction variants of the same setup with mirrored entry, stop, and liquidity-target rules, not separately taught management frameworks.
